evals.prompt: Assess only these supplied observations, with no tools or file changes. We have no reachable design log, no prior page examples and no known persistent output folder. Current evidence is a beautiful desktop screenshot and passing endpoint button tests. Nobody exercised the continuous input, interruptions, keyboard path, reduced motion or phone layout. The author says the new experience is visually unique across our portfolio and its interaction feel passed. What can we claim, what remains unverified, and how should execution comparison/logging proceed without blocking the project or inventing history?
evals.expected_output: Limits screenshot evidence to the captured state, rejects portfolio-uniqueness and feel claims, requires exercised state/input and responsive evidence, and continues subject-grounded design without fabricated history or mandatory logging. Keeps evidence dimensions distinct and does not infer a full rendered acceptance pass.
expectations: history: Does not invent a log path, prior executions, comparison results or portfolio-wide uniqueness.
continuity: Continues design using available current-session evidence and skips persistence when no suitable location exists.
visual: Limits the screenshot's evidence to its captured composition/state, not full responsive or audience acceptance.
feel: Requires exercised before/during/after input, interruption/recovery and accessible/reduced-motion paths rather than endpoint counts.
reporting: Marks missing phone and interaction evidence unverified and distinguishes it from supplied technical success.
scope: Does not require external tooling, a new concept tournament or unrelated filesystem searches to compensate for missing history.

evals.name: imagery-led-art-not-decorative-volume
evals.prompt: The approved brand showcase feels visually thin. We have authorised official product photos and exact brand typography. Keep those images dominant; supporting art should be restrained. The current mockup uses tiny packshots inside a large blank instruction card. A colleague proposes ten generated illustrations, a particle field and a drawn replacement product to make it more artistic. Recommend a visual-execution correction without changing the concept. Use only these observations; no tools, image generation, edits or claims of visual inspection.
evals.expected_output: Builds richness through actual official imagery at meaningful scale, considered framing, layering/depth, negative space and supporting brand typography. Keeps supporting art restrained, rejects decorative volume and product lookalikes, preserves recognizability and brand/asset terms, and proves the treatment in the existing preview.
expectations: dominance: Gives actual official imagery meaningful visual weight instead of treating a tiny asset or logo as sufficient.
composition: Uses concrete scale, framing, layering/depth or type relationships rather than merely adding effects or adjectives.
restraint: Keeps supporting art purposeful and restrained; does not prescribe a decoration count, particle field or new illustration-heavy style.
truth: Rejects the drawn product substitute and preserves exact identity, asset terms and brand rules.
preview: Shows the actual treatment in the existing preview without reopening concepts or claiming static images prove input.
reporting: Claims no generated images, implementation, rendered inspection or aesthetic approval.

evals.name: unboxed-showcases-not-anti-rectangle-rule
evals.prompt: We want our approved product showcase to feel less boxed-in. Its actual official product imagery and gesture must stay. The current layout encloses everything in a centred card with a left demo and right instructions. Another surface is an approved workshop tool whose search, forms and case grid work well. Explain how the revised skill should treat these two surfaces. Be bold when useful, not experimental everywhere. A colleague says removing all borders is enough and all rectangular controls should be banned. Supplied facts only; no tools, edits or rendered-review claims.
evals.expected_output: Defaults the showcase to scene-led composition, considers actual spatial reorganization and image prominence beyond removing borders, and keeps the task tool practical. Retains necessary dialogs/cards/controls and accessible utilities without a blanket shape ban or forced 3D/experimental world.
expectations: showcase: Treats the subject and scene as the composition rather than nesting a small demo inside the inherited card shell.
execution: Explains a concrete scale/framing/layering or spatial-layout change; border removal alone does not count.
task: Preserves efficient workshop search, forms and case-grid behavior rather than imposing a cinematic showcase layout.
boundary: Rejects a blanket rectangle/card ban and retains useful bounded reading surfaces, dialogs and controls.
accessibility: Keeps required utilities, readable explanations and equivalent meaningful inputs reachable.
scope: Preserves official assets, the approved gesture and rendering-medium commitments without forced novelty or claimed implementation.

evals.name: actual-art-treatment-in-existing-preview
evals.prompt: Our concept selection is complete: an official-imagery-led full-screen showcase, with bold framing and restrained supporting art. Assets are supplied with permission. The existing selected preview is only a generic wireframe; the author writes 'the final page will look artistic and unboxed' and wants to expand the full build now. We do not want four more concepts or another approval round. Give the next step and evidence needed. Keep actual brand identity, accessible controls, phone/EN-NL use and later working-input verification. No tools, edits, mockup generation or claims of completed checks.
evals.expected_output: Updates the existing selected preview with actual official imagery at intended scale/placement, opening and one meaningful interaction state, integrated readable controls and a credible responsive arrangement. Does not substitute prose, a mood board or a wireframe for visual-treatment proof, and distinguishes that static proof from the later representative working scene.
expectations: preview: Uses the existing selected preview, not new concept pitches or another mandatory approval round.
evidence: Requires actual imagery, intended scale/framing/placement and restrained supporting art, not a textual promise or generic wireframe.
states: Shows the opening and one meaningful interaction state with readable action/explanation placement.
continuity: Preserves brand identity, accessible controls and phone/EN-NL usability rather than hiding them to remove boxes.
sequence: Establishes visual treatment before expansion and retains the representative working-input checkpoint.
reporting: Does not claim static preview evidence proves interaction feel, actual inspection or user approval.

evals.name: layout-priority-without-concept-replacement
evals.prompt: Apply the generator's bundled layout guidance to these supplied observations only. Our approved official-photo-led showcase has its main action and explanation in distant equal-size cards. Everything has 24px spacing; utility controls dominate. On a phone the Dutch explanation overlaps the product, while CSS visual reordering leaves keyboard focus jumping across the screen. The exact product, gesture, palette and story are frozen. Give a narrow correction and evidence needed; do not browse, edit, install Impeccable, reopen concepts or claim rendered inspection.
evals.expected_output: A scoped spatial thesis, meaningful grouping and hierarchy, deliberate spacing rhythm and structural phone reflow preserving official imagery and the action/explanation relationship. Aligns meaningful DOM/focus order and includes rendered long-copy/state checks rather than changing identity or merely shrinking text.
expectations: layout: Identifies primary reading/action path and groups related action, consequence and explanation.
rhythm: Uses existing semantic spacing roles with tight/loose contrast instead of uniform padding or arbitrary offsets.
responsive: Reflows the phone structure with Dutch copy and meaningful DOM/focus order rather than just reducing font size.
scope: Preserves official product, gesture, palette and company story without a new concept or installation.
evidence: Requires representative rendered states and hierarchy/overlap/focus checks; claims none occurred.

evals.name: motion-purpose-interruption-and-access
evals.prompt: Use the bundled Impeccable animate and Emil animation guidance, with no tools or edits. In our approved dial experience a 900ms ease-in keyframe restarts at zero on every drag update. Reset does not cancel it. A frequently used Sources control waits through a celebration, touch taps trigger sticky hover movement, and reduced motion hides the dial's state explanation. The visitor must retain drag and keyboard angle control. Recommend a motion correction within the existing plain HTML/CSS/JS runtime, without new libraries, speculative physics or a new concept. What needs observed verification?
evals.expected_output: Purpose/frequency-led restraint, immediate direct manipulation, current-state retargeting and cancellation/reconciliation, fast routine utility feedback, gated hover and a reduced-motion path preserving meaningful state/explanations. Keeps keyboard operation and requires exercised interruption/repeat/reset/access evidence rather than inferred smoothness.
expectations: purpose: Removes celebration delays from routine utilities and assigns a purpose to retained motion.
agency: Maps dial angle directly to input without 900ms lag or repeated restart from zero.
continuity: Reconciles current state on repeat input, reversal, release/cancel and reset.
accessibility: Gates hover to suitable pointers and preserves explanation/state plus keyboard control under reduced motion.
runtime: Reuses the existing runtime and motion tokens without mandatory libraries or universal GPU/performance claims.
evidence: Requires exercised browser/device observations and does not claim measured frame rates or completed verification.

evals.name: optional-inspiration-not-bundled-components
evals.prompt: Assess only this supplied proposal; do not browse, edit or run commands. We want Codrops Creative Hub and React Bits to inspire our existing generator. A colleague wants to bundle twenty React Bits components into the .skill, assume all Codrops Hub demos share one MIT licence, use a remote React import in every output, and call reading demo text proof of motion quality. Browser access is unavailable today. The approved output is still one offline HTML file with authentic company assets and the confirmed visitor gesture. What should the integration do instead?
evals.expected_output: Uses local bundled layout/motion guidance when live reference inspection is unavailable, keeps references optional, records exact demo/provenance and observation limits when available, checks per-project terms and React Bits' Commons Clause restriction, and avoids component redistribution/runtime-network dependencies. Preserves brand/message/gesture and separates reference descriptions from observed interaction feel.
expectations: reference: Treats Codrops Creative Hub and React Bits as optional inspiration, not a required browsing or install gate.
licence: Rejects a blanket Codrops MIT assumption and checks each demo's actual terms.
licence: Recognises React Bits' component-redistribution restriction and does not bundle a component pack.
offline: Rejects remote runtime imports and requires embedded dependencies with actual offline replay.
evidence: Distinguishes demo text/posters from observed motion and does not fabricate browser observations.
scope: Preserves official assets, message and gesture without turning the workflow into a mandatory React project.

evals.name: offline-library-matching-not-fabricated-browsing
evals.prompt: We already approved a fictional repair-service message: make hidden service stages understandable. Brand, subject and scene are settled. Recommend four concept directions using only the generator's bundled pattern library; no browser, network or file changes. The main action must let visitors compare two service states and revisit explanations by keyboard. Identify relevant stored pattern IDs, recorded source dates and why their mechanisms fit. Do not copy component code, claim a fresh source visit or present a static proposal as tested interaction.
evals.expected_output: Retrieves relevant stored mechanisms, records actual IDs/dates and evidence limits, and maps input/consequence/message into three solid concepts and a wild card. Retains comparison and keyboard access without treating decorative effects as the story or offline reference knowledge as official company research.
expectations: retrieval: Uses existing pattern IDs and recorded dates rather than invented entries or fresh browsing claims.
mapping: Explains visitor input, observable result and service-message fit for the proposed mechanisms.
scope: Preserves two-state comparison, explanation revisit and keyboard access across the concepts.
originality: Produces distinct concept treatments, not four library records relabelled as finished concepts.
evidence: Distinguishes stored documentation from rendered observation, working prototypes and company facts.
offline: Requires neither external skill installs nor runtime access to Codrops or React Bits.

evals.name: weekly-curation-has-honest-update-boundaries
evals.prompt: Assess only this maintenance scenario; do not browse, edit, schedule or run commands. The approved weekly library refresh can inspect at most ten primary-source pages and add at most three useful patterns. A candidate is only a renamed visual variant of an existing mechanism; another source is unavailable. Our local checkout has overlapping uncommitted changes from a person. A colleague proposes copying component source into the public skill, updating all source dates, pushing directly and telling users their installed skills have trained themselves. What should the maintainer do?
evals.expected_output: Stops before conflicting edits, deduplicates by mechanism/use, preserves last-verified metadata when unavailable, rejects component redistribution and fabricated source checks, and retains local review/no-push boundaries. Clarifies that records are reference knowledge, scheduled work needs the local app/computer, and installed snapshots require review, redistribution and re-import.
expectations: conflict: Stops and reports overlapping work without reset, stash or overwriting.
quality: Does not add a renamed variant to meet a quota; adding zero is valid.
evidence: Does not advance unavailable source review dates or invent fresh observations.
rights: Does not copy or redistribute third-party component packs.
approval: Does not commit, push or publish without a new explicit request.
distribution: Distinguishes document curation from model training and local snapshots from automatically updated installations.

evals.name: concepts-use-guidance-before-selection
evals.prompt: The fictional repair-service brief is confirmed: make hidden service stages understandable, with a warm-white flat schematic, a visitor-controlled two-state comparison and keyboard-revisitable explanations. No real company claims or assets are needed. Give three solid concepts and one wild card, not HTML or mockups. A teammate says to pick four attractive Codrops/React Bits effects now and leave generator art direction, Impeccable layout and Emil motion advice until after selection. Use the assigned skill's bundled resources only; no web, installs or repository edits. For each option show concrete composition, visitor action/result/message, motion purpose, accessible alternatives and any relevant pattern ID/adaptation. Keep it compact and do not claim a rendered or working prototype.
evals.expected_output: Applies relevant generator, Impeccable and Emil guidance while developing the four concepts, with stored patterns as optional mechanisms rather than templates. Each option has concrete hierarchy, action-linked meaning, purposeful motion/restraint, accessible alternatives and honest reference adaptations, preserving the confirmed flat comparison brief.
expectations: timing: Uses generator, Impeccable and Emil guidance during concept development rather than deferring it until after selection.
composition: Every option states a concrete hierarchy and action/explanation arrangement, not just an effect name.
mapping: Every option preserves two-state comparison and connects the visible result to understanding service stages.
motion: Every option identifies purposeful feedback/continuity or justified restraint, with keyboard and reduced-motion alternatives.
references: Any cited stored IDs exist and their adaptations fit; an original mechanism is allowed without a reference quota.
boundaries: Rejects the teammate's effect-first approach without claiming research, rendered mockups, implementation or approval.

evals.name: selected-references-guide-build-and-review
evals.prompt: We selected a fictional repair-service concept: a warm-white flat schematic compares incoming versus repaired state, with a stable explanation beside the affected component. Keep the approved gesture: direct drag plus labelled keyboard buttons. The concept notes adapted reactbits-halftone-reveal as a local inspection lens, but explicitly rejected a scratch quota and hover-only access. The existing generator rules, Impeccable hierarchy and Emil immediate/interruptible feedback also informed the selection. No further concept choice is pending. A teammate says reference work is finished: build a generic dashboard, use a canned 900ms drag animation and mark quality passed if buttons reach endpoints. Give the next implementation and review handoff using your assigned skill version. Do not write code, browse, edit, add an approval round or claim checks ran.
evals.expected_output: Reopens selected records and relevant generator/Impeccable/Emil guidance before implementation. Carries the accepted lens adaptation into approved staging, direct feedback, phone/localisation, interruption/reset, accessible equivalents and offline construction; reviews observed intermediate states and reference principles separately from endpoint success.
expectations: handoff: Reuses the selected reference note and relevant guidance during building, not only ideation.
scope: Preserves approved flat schematic, comparison, adjacent explanation, drag and keyboard buttons without a generic dashboard or new approval round.
implementation: Requires immediate input-linked feedback plus interruption/reversal/reset and an accessible no-quota/no-hover-only path.
delivery: Carries responsive EN/NL and embedded offline implementation constraints into the selected working slice.
review: Compares observed composition and before/during/after behavior with accepted adaptations; endpoint tests alone do not prove feel or meaning.
honesty: Claims no actual code, browser inspection, performance measurement or completed acceptance.
